To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

young women with breast cancer are more likely than their older counterparts to develop premature menopause following breast cancer treatment, and that this premature menopause has a significant negative impact on QOL.
young breast cancer survivors experience a wide range of symptoms related to premature menopause, and that these symptoms can adversely affect health-related and psychologic quality of life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of premature menopause on the QOL of young women with breast cancer and with the efficacy of interventions to improve QOL in these young survivors.
the effects of premature menopause on the quality of life of young breast cancer survivors and the efficacy of treatment interventions for these symptoms.
the impact of adjuvant treatment-induced premature menopause on QOL and treatment interventions in young breast cancer patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

premature menopause in young women with breast cancer is associated with significant adverse effects on quality of health and quality of life and that these effects are not well understood or adequately managed.
the use of adjuvant chemotherapy in premenopausal women with breast cancer is associated with an increased risk of premature ovarian insufficiency.
there is a need for more research on the use of non-pharmacologic and pharmacologic interventions to relieve menopause symptoms in young breast cancer patients and to improve QOL.

the majority of the women in our study were experiencing menopause symptoms and had not received any type of intervention for these symptoms.
there are few data available about the prevalence of menopausal symptoms in young breast cancer patients and even fewer data about the impact these symptoms have on quality of life.
we need to better understand the needs and preferences of young breast cancer survivors, and then develop and test interventions that are tailored to these needs.

there is a need for more data on the use and efficacy for interventions in young breast cancer patients who become menopausual as a result of treatment.
